name: Costa Rica
summary: Costa Rica taxes individuals only on Costa Rican-source income, so a foreign portfolio's dividends and gains are not taxed locally. Local capital gains and dividends are taxed at 15%. There is no inheritance, gift or net wealth tax; property tax is 0.25% plus a luxury home tax on expensive homes. Foreign passive income held through a Costa Rican company in a multinational group can be taxed.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence (territorial)
regimes.description: Individuals are taxed only on Costa Rican-source income. Foreign dividends, interest and gains are not taxed for individuals. Costa Rican-source capital gains and dividends 15%.
regimes.eligibility: Permanent residents and individuals present six months or more in a tax year are resident.

capital_gains.summary: Costa Rican-source capital gains are taxed at 15% (Law 7092 as amended by Law 9635), with an option of 2.25% of the sale price on the first sale of an asset under certain conditions. Foreign-source gains of individuals are outside the territorial scope.

sources.title: Deloitte International Tax: Costa Rica Highlights 2026
PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Costa Rica, Individual - Income determination
PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Costa Rica, Individual - Taxes on personal income

capital_gains.rate_basis: 15% capital gains rate (Deloitte 2026; PwC reviewed 30 Jun 2026). Foreign gains 0 under the territorial principle (PwC: Costa Rica-source income = assets used, goods located, services rendered in Costa Rica).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Real estate transfer tax 1.5% (PwC). Gains realised habitually in a business are taxed at ordinary rates up to 25%/30%.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Not taxed for individuals. For companies in multinational groups, foreign passive income can be taxed (non-qualified entity rule) - relevant if the portfolio is held through a Costa Rican company.
open_questions: Conditions of the 2.25% option (assets acquired before 1 Jul 2019?) not verified.
Status of any 2025/2026 bill to move to worldwide ('renta global') taxation not checked (web search budget exhausted).

dividends.summary: Dividends from Costa Rican companies: 15% final withholding. Foreign dividends of individuals are not taxed.

sources.title: Deloitte International Tax: Costa Rica Highlights 2026
PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Costa Rica, Individual - Taxes on personal income

dividends.rate_basis: Deloitte 2026: 15% WHT on dividends paid to resident individuals; territorial principle for foreign income.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 15% (5% for listed stock corporations paying non-residents); treaty reductions.
dividends.treaty_network: Four treaties in force (Germany, Mexico, Spain, UAE). No US treaty.
open_questions: No source explicitly addressed foreign portfolio dividends for individuals; inferred from the territorial rule.

sources.title: Deloitte International Tax: Costa Rica Highlights 2026

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipal property tax 0.25% of value; a separate annual luxury home tax (impuesto solidario) applies to high-value homes (rates not verified).

inheritance.summary: No inheritance, estate or gift tax.

sources.title: Deloitte International Tax: Costa Rica Highlights 2026

inheritance.important_exceptions: Registration/transfer costs on Costa Rican real estate (1.5% transfer tax on sales).

residency.tax_residency_test: Permanent residents, or presence for six months or more in the tax year (Deloitte 2026).

routes.name: Rentista / Inversionista / Pensionado residence
routes.requirements: Costa Rica has income- and investment-based residence categories; current thresholds not verified.

sources.title: Deloitte International Tax: Costa Rica Highlights 2026

corporate.summary: CIT 30% (reduced rates for small companies); territorial, except foreign passive income of 'non-qualified' entities in multinational groups, taxed (dividends and gains generally 15%).

sources.title: Deloitte International Tax: Costa Rica Highlights 2026
PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Costa Rica, Corporate - Income determination

prime_rent_monthly.description: Escazú, 4+ bedroom apartment, monthly asking rent in Global Property Guide's Q2 2026 survey (purchase price of the same unit type USD 600,000; gross yield 5.40%). An apartment, not a detached villa: large gated houses in Escazú or Santa Ana are likely to rent for more.

source.title: Global Property Guide: Costa Rica rental yields (Q2 2026)

intl_school_annual_fee.description: Country Day School (Escazú), grade 12, 2026-27: yearly tuition USD 22,015 plus the annual matriculation fee of USD 1,300. One-off fees for new students (entrance USD 2,500 per student, family fee USD 1,000) are excluded. Grades 9-11 tuition is USD 21,931.

source.title: Country Day School Costa Rica: Tuition and fees 2026-2027

cost_of_living.notes: Price per m2, health insurance and housekeeper not sourced in this pass. Rents and school fees are quoted in USD.

us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain subject to US federal income, estate and gift tax on worldwide income and assets; the app adds the federal layer. Local tax can generally be credited against US tax on the same foreign-source income only where the US foreign tax credit rules allow.
open_questions: Global income reform status (2025/2026) not verified.
Luxury home tax rates not verified.
